+## Abstract
 
-Let X_Gamma^+ be a mixing one-sided edge shift, let G be finite, and let a
-one-step cocycle label each primitive orbit gamma by a conjugacy class
-[g_gamma]. We determine the constant in the Frobenius-class Mertens product
-by separating the periodic Artin logarithm from the fixed-label Euler
-transform. The former powers the primitive label under repetition, whereas
-the latter repeats the scalar weight while keeping the primitive label fixed.
-Under the strict twisted spectral gap, we prove an Adams--Mobius determinant
-formula for F_rho(lambda^{-1}) and hence for every class-product constant.
-This gives two corrections to the theorem of Mohamed and Noorani (1999).
-Mixing of the base alone does not imply uniform Frobenius density, so an
-extension-level transitivity/aperiodicity condition, imposed here as the
-strict twisted gap, is required for the exponent |C|/|G|. Under this
-hypothesis, their constant also replaces chi_rho(g_gamma) by
-chi_rho(g_gamma^r) in the r-th logarithmic term. A trivial C_2-cocycle
-exhibits the first defect, while a strict-gap S_3 extension exhibits the
-second: its sign Artin logarithm vanishes although its fixed-label coordinate
-is strictly negative. We also give the corrected union-of-classes constant
-for the homogeneous-extension consequence.
+Let E=(C2)^r, and let two one-step E-cocycles lie over primitive edge shifts
+whose vertex counts are at most V; the base shifts need not be the same. For
+the primitive length-element counts p_(n,g), put E_g(y)=sum_(n>=1)
+p_(n,g) log(1-y^n). Without a twisted-gap hypothesis, equality of every
+element profile at 2V ceil(log_2(4V)) distinct radii in the common open Perron
+interval forces equality of every p_(n,g), provided that one sampled radius
+is algebraic. Thus the number of radial locations is independent of r,
+although each location supplies the full 2^r-component profile vector. For a
+reduced binary character-determinant ratio of total degree D>0, one algebraic
+collision identifies the complete real collision set, which has at most
+D ceil(log_2(2D))-1 points. The inverse mechanism is arithmetic: determinant
+parity, Nishioka's special-value theorem, and Nishioka's algebraic-solution
+rationality theorem force a normalized rational Mahler coboundary. A divisor
+l1 estimate gives an O(D log D) degree bound and one finite Pade system
+reconstructs or rejects the certificate. An exact four-vertex pair shows that
+one centered Perron-boundary profile vector does not suffice. For general
+finite groups, recovery holds from a radial set with an interior accumulation
+point; already for C3, Adams--Mobius inversion exhibits the obstruction to a
+finite bound by coupling determinant logarithms at infinitely many powers.

+Dear Editors,
+
+We submit "Prime support and multiple-context-free languages in recurrent
+numeration" for consideration as an Original Research Article in Monatshefte
+fuer Mathematik.
+
+The article studies prime-support obstructions for canonical languages in
+eventually recurrent numeration systems. Its main results combine weak
+multiple-context-free pumping with the affine recurrence action, adic
+topology, and recurrence arithmetic. The manuscript is mathematically
+self-contained; none of its theorem proofs depends on a numbered result in
+the Supplementary Information.
+
+The submission includes two referee-facing online resources. Online Resource
+1 is the separately compiled Supplementary Information PDF containing the
+independent finite-state, Zeckendorf, and analytic comparisons described in
+the article. Online Resource 2 is the reproducibility archive containing the
+Python verifier, its unit tests, archived verifier and test outputs, the
+literature audit, checksums, and reproduction instructions. We ask that both
+online resources be made available to the referees with the main manuscript.
+
+The manuscript is not under consideration elsewhere. All authors have
+approved the submission. The authors declare no competing interests. No
+research datasets were generated or analysed.

+Let E=(C2)^r, and let two one-step E-cocycles lie over primitive edge shifts
+whose vertex counts are at most V; the base shifts need not be the same. For
+the primitive length-element counts p_(n,g), put E_g(y)=sum_(n>=1)
+p_(n,g) log(1-y^n). Without a twisted-gap hypothesis, equality of every
+element profile at 2V ceil(log_2(4V)) distinct radii in the common open Perron

+is algebraic. Thus the number of radial locations is independent of r,
+although each location supplies the full 2^r-component profile vector. For a
+reduced binary character-determinant ratio of total degree D>0, one algebraic
+collision identifies the complete real collision set, which has at most
+D ceil(log_2(2D))-1 points. The inverse mechanism is arithmetic: determinant
+parity, Nishioka's special-value theorem, and Nishioka's algebraic-solution

+l1 estimate gives an O(D log D) degree bound and one finite Pade system
+reconstructs or rejects the certificate. An exact four-vertex pair shows that
+one centered Perron-boundary profile vector does not suffice. For general
+finite groups, recovery holds from a radial set with an interior accumulation
+point; already for C3, Adams--Mobius inversion exhibits the obstruction to a
+finite bound by coupling determinant logarithms at infinitely many powers.

+Dear Editors,
+
+We submit "Prime support and multiple-context-free languages in recurrent
+numeration" for consideration as an Original Research Article in Monatshefte
+fuer Mathematik.
+
+The article studies prime-support obstructions for canonical languages in
+eventually recurrent numeration systems. Its main results combine weak
+multiple-context-free pumping with the affine recurrence action, adic
+topology, and recurrence arithmetic. The manuscript is mathematically
+self-contained; none of its theorem proofs depends on a numbered result in
+the Supplementary Information.
+
+The submission includes two referee-facing online resources. Online Resource
+1 is the separately compiled Supplementary Information PDF containing the
+independent finite-state, Zeckendorf, and analytic comparisons described in
+the article. Online Resource 2 is the reproducibility archive containing the
+Python verifier, its unit tests, archived verifier and test outputs, the
+literature audit, checksums, and reproduction instructions. We ask that both
+online resources be made available to the referees with the main manuscript.

$utf8 = New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding($false)
function Split-TexFile {
    param([string]$Path, [int[]]$CutLines, [string[]]$PartNames)
    $full = [IO.Path]::GetFullPath($Path)
    $sourceText = [IO.File]::ReadAllText($full)
    $starts = [regex]::Matches($sourceText, '"'(?m)"'^'"')
    "'$positions = @(0)
    foreach ($line in $CutLines) {
        $positions += $starts[$line - 1].Index
    }
    $positions += $sourceText.Length
    $parts = @()
    for ($i = 0; $i -lt $PartNames.Count; $i++) {
        $parts += $sourceText.Substring($positions[$i], $positions[$i + 1] - $positions[$i])
        [IO.File]::WriteAllText((Join-Path ([IO.Path]::GetDirectoryName($full)) $PartNames[$i]), $parts[$i], $utf8)
    }
    if (($parts -join '"'') -cne "'$sourceText) { throw "content mismatch while splitting $Path" }
    $wrapperLines = $PartNames | ForEach-Object { '"'\\input{' + [IO.Path]::GetFileNameWithoutExtension("'$_) + '"'}' }
    "'$wrapper = ($wrapperLines -join [Environment]::NewLine) + [Environment]::NewLine
    [IO.File]::WriteAllText($full, $wrapper, $utf8)
    $partCounts = $PartNames | ForEach-Object { ([IO.File]::ReadAllLines((Join-Path ([IO.Path]::GetDirectoryName($full)) $_))).Count }
    "SPLIT $Path -> $($PartNames -join '"', ') lines="'$($partCounts -join '"',') content_equal=True\"
}

+## Abstract
 
-Let X_Gamma^+ be a mixing one-sided edge shift, let G be finite, and let a
-one-step cocycle label each primitive orbit gamma by a conjugacy class
-[g_gamma]. We determine the constant in the Frobenius-class Mertens product
-by separating the periodic Artin logarithm from the fixed-label Euler
-transform. The former powers the primitive label under repetition, whereas
-the latter repeats the scalar weight while keeping the primitive label fixed.
-Under the strict twisted spectral gap, we prove an Adams--Mobius determinant
-formula for F_rho(lambda^{-1}) and hence for every class-product constant.
-This gives two corrections to the theorem of Mohamed and Noorani (1999).
-Mixing of the base alone does not imply uniform Frobenius density, so an
-extension-level transitivity/aperiodicity condition, imposed here as the
-strict twisted gap, is required for the exponent |C|/|G|. Under this
-hypothesis, their constant also replaces chi_rho(g_gamma) by
-chi_rho(g_gamma^r) in the r-th logarithmic term. A trivial C_2-cocycle
-exhibits the first defect, while a strict-gap S_3 extension exhibits the
-second: its sign Artin logarithm vanishes although its fixed-label coordinate
-is strictly negative. We also give the corrected union-of-classes constant
-for the homogeneous-extension consequence.
+Let E=(C2)^r, and let two one-step E-cocycles lie over primitive edge shifts
+whose vertex counts are at most V; the base shifts need not be the same. For
+the primitive length-element counts p_(n,g), put E_g(y)=sum_(n>=1)
+p_(n,g) log(1-y^n). Without a twisted-gap hypothesis, equality of every
+element profile at 2V ceil(log_2(4V)) distinct radii in the common open Perron
+interval forces equality of every p_(n,g), provided that one sampled radius
+is algebraic. Thus the number of radial locations is independent of r,
+although each location supplies the full 2^r-component profile vector. For a
+reduced binary character-determinant ratio of total degree D>0, one algebraic
+collision identifies the complete real collision set, which has at most
+D ceil(log_2(2D))-1 points. The inverse mechanism is arithmetic: determinant
+parity, Nishioka's special-value theorem, and Nishioka's algebraic-solution
+rationality theorem force a normalized rational Mahler coboundary. A divisor
+l1 estimate gives an O(D log D) degree bound and one finite Pade system
+reconstructs or rejects the certificate. An exact four-vertex pair shows that
+one centered Perron-boundary profile vector does not suffice. For general
+finite groups, recovery holds from a radial set with an interior accumulation
+point; already for C3, Adams--Mobius inversion exhibits the obstruction to a
+finite bound by coupling determinant logarithms at infinitely many powers.

+Dear Editors,
+
+We submit "Prime support and multiple-context-free languages in recurrent
+numeration" for consideration as an Original Research Article in Monatshefte
+fuer Mathematik.
+
+The article studies prime-support obstructions for canonical languages in
+eventually recurrent numeration systems. Its main results combine weak
+multiple-context-free pumping with the affine recurrence action, adic
+topology, and recurrence arithmetic. The manuscript is mathematically
+self-contained; none of its theorem proofs depends on a numbered result in
+the Supplementary Information.
+
+The submission includes two referee-facing online resources. Online Resource
+1 is the separately compiled Supplementary Information PDF containing the
+independent finite-state, Zeckendorf, and analytic comparisons described in
+the article. Online Resource 2 is the reproducibility archive containing the
+Python verifier, its unit tests, archived verifier and test outputs, the
+literature audit, checksums, and reproduction instructions. We ask that both
+online resources be made available to the referees with the main manuscript.
+
+The manuscript is not under consideration elsewhere. All authors have
+approved the submission. The authors declare no competing interests. No
+research datasets were generated or analysed.

+## Abstract
 
-Let X_Gamma^+ be a mixing one-sided edge shift, let G be finite, and let a
-one-step cocycle label each primitive orbit gamma by a conjugacy class

-This gives two corrections to the theorem of Mohamed and Noorani (1999).

+Let E=(C2)^r, and let two one-step E-cocycles lie over primitive edge shifts
+whose vertex counts are at most V; the base shifts need not be the same. For
+the primitive length-element counts p_(n,g), put E_g(y)=sum_(n>=1)
+p_(n,g) log(1-y^n). Without a twisted-gap hypothesis, equality of every
+element profile at 2V ceil(log_2(4V)) distinct radii in the common open Perron
+interval forces equality of every p_(n,g), provided that one sampled radius
+is algebraic. Thus the number of radial locations is independent of r,
+although each location supplies the full 2^r-component profile vector. For a
+reduced binary character-determinant ratio of total degree D>0, one algebraic
+collision identifies the complete real collision set, which has at most
+D ceil(log_2(2D))-1 points. The inverse mechanism is arithmetic: determinant
+parity, Nishioka's special-value theorem, and Nishioka's algebraic-solution
+rationality theorem force a normalized rational Mahler coboundary. A divisor
+l1 estimate gives an O(D log D) degree bound and one finite Pade system
+reconstructs or rejects the certificate. An exact four-vertex pair shows that
+one centered Perron-boundary profile vector does not suffice. For general
+finite groups, recovery holds from a radial set with an interior accumulation
+point; already for C3, Adams--Mobius inversion exhibits the obstruction to a
+finite bound by coupling determinant logarithms at infinitely many powers.

+Dear Editors,
+
+We submit "Prime support and multiple-context-free languages in recurrent
+numeration" for consideration as an Original Research Article in Monatshefte
+fuer Mathematik.
+
+The article studies prime-support obstructions for canonical languages in
+eventually recurrent numeration systems. Its main results combine weak
+multiple-context-free pumping with the affine recurrence action, adic
+topology, and recurrence arithmetic. The manuscript is mathematically
+self-contained; none of its theorem proofs depends on a numbered result in
+the Supplementary Information.
+
+The submission includes two referee-facing online resources. Online Resource
+1 is the separately compiled Supplementary Information PDF containing the
+independent finite-state, Zeckendorf, and analytic comparisons described in
+the article. Online Resource 2 is the reproducibility archive containing the
+Python verifier, its unit tests, archived verifier and test outputs, the
+literature audit, checksums, and reproduction instructions. We ask that both
+online resources be made available to the referees with the main manuscript.

+## Abstract
 
-Let X_Gamma^+ be a mixing one-sided edge shift, let G be finite, and let a
-one-step cocycle label each primitive orbit gamma by a conjugacy class
-[g_gamma]. We determine the constant in the Frobenius-class Mertens product
-by separating the periodic Artin logarithm from the fixed-label Euler
-transform. The former powers the primitive label under repetition, whereas
-the latter repeats the scalar weight while keeping the primitive label fixed.
-Under the strict twisted spectral gap, we prove an Adams--Mobius determinant
-formula for F_rho(lambda^{-1}) and hence for every class-product constant.
-This gives two corrections to the theorem of Mohamed and Noorani (1999).
-Mixing of the base alone does not imply uniform Frobenius density, so an
-extension-level transitivity/aperiodicity condition, imposed here as the
-strict twisted gap, is required for the exponent |C|/|G|. Under this
-hypothesis, their constant also replaces chi_rho(g_gamma) by

+Let E=(C2)^r, and let two one-step E-cocycles lie over primitive edge shifts
+whose vertex counts are at most V; the base shifts need not be the same. For
+the primitive length-element counts p_(n,g), put E_g(y)=sum_(n>=1)
+p_(n,g) log(1-y^n). Without a twisted-gap hypothesis, equality of every
+element profile at 2V ceil(log_2(4V)) distinct radii in the common open Perron
+interval forces equality of every p_(n,g), provided that one sampled radius
+is algebraic. Thus the number of radial locations is independent of r,
+although each location supplies the full 2^r-component profile vector. For a
+reduced binary character-determinant ratio of total degree D>0, one algebraic
+collision identifies the complete real collision set, which has at most
+D ceil(log_2(2D))-1 points. The inverse mechanism is arithmetic: determinant
+parity, Nishioka's special-value theorem, and Nishioka's algebraic-solution
+rationality theorem force a normalized rational Mahler coboundary. A divisor
+l1 estimate gives an O(D log D) degree bound and one finite Pade system
+reconstructs or rejects the certificate. An exact four-vertex pair shows that
+one centered Perron-boundary profile vector does not suffice. For general
+finite groups, recovery holds from a radial set with an interior accumulation
+point; already for C3, Adams--Mobius inversion exhibits the obstruction to a
+finite bound by coupling determinant logarithms at infinitely many powers.

+We submit "Prime support and multiple-context-free languages in recurrent
+numeration" for consideration as an Original Research Article in Monatshefte
+fuer Mathematik.
+
+The article studies prime-support obstructions for canonical languages in
+eventually recurrent numeration systems. Its main results combine weak
+multiple-context-free pumping with the affine recurrence action, adic
+topology, and recurrence arithmetic. The manuscript is mathematically
+self-contained; none of its theorem proofs depends on a numbered result in
+the Supplementary Information.

+Let E=(C2)^r, and let two one-step E-cocycles lie over primitive edge shifts
+whose vertex counts are at most V; the base shifts need not be the same. For
+the primitive length-element counts p_(n,g), put E_g(y)=sum_(n>=1)
+p_(n,g) log(1-y^n). Without a twisted-gap hypothesis, equality of every
+element profile at 2V ceil(log_2(4V)) distinct radii in the common open Perron
+interval forces equality of every p_(n,g), provided that one sampled radius
+is algebraic. Thus the number of radial locations is independent of r,
+although each location supplies the full 2^r-component profile vector. For a
+reduced binary character-determinant ratio of total degree D>0, one algebraic
+collision identifies the complete real collision set, which has at most
+D ceil(log_2(2D))-1 points. The inverse mechanism is arithmetic: determinant
+parity, Nishioka's special-value theorem, and Nishioka's algebraic-solution
+rationality theorem force a normalized rational Mahler coboundary. A divisor
+l1 estimate gives an O(D log D) degree bound and one finite Pade system
+reconstructs or rejects the certificate. An exact four-vertex pair shows that
+one centered Perron-boundary profile vector does not suffice. For general
+finite groups, recovery holds from a radial set with an interior accumulation
+point; already for C3, Adams--Mobius inversion exhibits the obstruction to a
+finite bound by coupling determinant logarithms at infinitely many powers.

+Dear Editors,
+
+We submit "Prime support and multiple-context-free languages in recurrent
+numeration" for consideration as an Original Research Article in Monatshefte
+fuer Mathematik.
+
+The article studies prime-support obstructions for canonical languages in
+eventually recurrent numeration systems. Its main results combine weak
+multiple-context-free pumping with the affine recurrence action, adic
+topology, and recurrence arithmetic. The manuscript is mathematically
+self-contained; none of its theorem proofs depends on a numbered result in
+the Supplementary Information.
+
+The submission includes two referee-facing online resources. Online Resource
+1 is the separately compiled Supplementary Information PDF containing the
+independent finite-state, Zeckendorf, and analytic comparisons described in
+the article. Online Resource 2 is the reproducibility archive containing the
+Python verifier, its unit tests, archived verifier and test outputs, the
+literature audit, checksums, and reproduction instructions. We ask that both
+online resources be made available to the referees with the main manuscript.
+
+The manuscript is not under consideration elsewhere. All authors have
+approved the submission. The authors declare no competing interests. No
+research datasets were generated or analysed.

-Mixing of the base alone does not imply uniform Frobenius density, so an

+Let E=(C2)^r, and let two one-step E-cocycles lie over primitive edge shifts
+whose vertex counts are at most V; the base shifts need not be the same. For
+the primitive length-element counts p_(n,g), put E_g(y)=sum_(n>=1)
+p_(n,g) log(1-y^n). Without a twisted-gap hypothesis, equality of every
+element profile at 2V ceil(log_2(4V)) distinct radii in the common open Perron
+interval forces equality of every p_(n,g), provided that one sampled radius
+is algebraic. Thus the number of radial locations is independent of r,
+although each location supplies the full 2^r-component profile vector. For a
+reduced binary character-determinant ratio of total degree D>0, one algebraic
+collision identifies the complete real collision set, which has at most
+D ceil(log_2(2D))-1 points. The inverse mechanism is arithmetic: determinant
+parity, Nishioka's special-value theorem, and Nishioka's algebraic-solution
+rationality theorem force a normalized rational Mahler coboundary. A divisor
+l1 estimate gives an O(D log D) degree bound and one finite Pade system
+reconstructs or rejects the certificate. An exact four-vertex pair shows that
+one centered Perron-boundary profile vector does not suffice. For general
+finite groups, recovery holds from a radial set with an interior accumulation
+point; already for C3, Adams--Mobius inversion exhibits the obstruction to a
+finite bound by coupling determinant logarithms at infinitely many powers.

+Dear Editors,
+
+We submit "Prime support and multiple-context-free languages in recurrent
+numeration" for consideration as an Original Research Article in Monatshefte
+fuer Mathematik.
+
+The article studies prime-support obstructions for canonical languages in
+eventually recurrent numeration systems. Its main results combine weak
+multiple-context-free pumping with the affine recurrence action, adic
+topology, and recurrence arithmetic. The manuscript is mathematically
+self-contained; none of its theorem proofs depends on a numbered result in
+the Supplementary Information.
+
+The submission includes two referee-facing online resources. Online Resource
+1 is the separately compiled Supplementary Information PDF containing the
+independent finite-state, Zeckendorf, and analytic comparisons described in
+the article. Online Resource 2 is the reproducibility archive containing the
+Python verifier, its unit tests, archived verifier and test outputs, the
+literature audit, checksums, and reproduction instructions. We ask that both
+online resources be made available to the referees with the main manuscript.
+
+The manuscript is not under consideration elsewhere. All authors have
+approved the submission. The authors declare no competing interests. No
+research datasets were generated or analysed.
+

+Haobo Ma

+National University of Singapore

+## Abstract
 
-Let X_Gamma^+ be a mixing one-sided edge shift, let G be finite, and let a
-one-step cocycle label each primitive orbit gamma by a conjugacy class
-[g_gamma]. We determine the constant in the Frobenius-class Mertens product
-by separating the periodic Artin logarithm from the fixed-label Euler

-the latter repeats the scalar weight while keeping the primitive label fixed.
-Under the strict twisted spectral gap, we prove an Adams--Mobius determinant
-formula for F_rho(lambda^{-1}) and hence for every class-product constant.
-This gives two corrections to the theorem of Mohamed and Noorani (1999).
-Mixing of the base alone does not imply uniform Frobenius density, so an
-extension-level transitivity/aperiodicity condition, imposed here as the
-strict twisted gap, is required for the exponent |C|/|G|. Under this
-hypothesis, their constant also replaces chi_rho(g_gamma) by
-chi_rho(g_gamma^r) in the r-th logarithmic term. A trivial C_2-cocycle

+Let E=(C2)^r, and let two one-step E-cocycles lie over primitive edge shifts
+whose vertex counts are at most V; the base shifts need not be the same. For
+the primitive length-element counts p_(n,g), put E_g(y)=sum_(n>=1)
+p_(n,g) log(1-y^n). Without a twisted-gap hypothesis, equality of every
+element profile at 2V ceil(log_2(4V)) distinct radii in the common open Perron
+interval forces equality of every p_(n,g), provided that one sampled radius
+is algebraic. Thus the number of radial locations is independent of r,
+although each location supplies the full 2^r-component profile vector. For a
+reduced binary character-determinant ratio of total degree D>0, one algebraic
+collision identifies the complete real collision set, which has at most
+D ceil(log_2(2D))-1 points. The inverse mechanism is arithmetic: determinant
+parity, Nishioka's special-value theorem, and Nishioka's algebraic-solution
+rationality theorem force a normalized rational Mahler coboundary. A divisor
+l1 estimate gives an O(D log D) degree bound and one finite Pade system
+reconstructs or rejects the certificate. An exact four-vertex pair shows that
+one centered Perron-boundary profile vector does not suffice. For general
+finite groups, recovery holds from a radial set with an interior accumulation
+point; already for C3, Adams--Mobius inversion exhibits the obstruction to a
+finite bound by coupling determinant logarithms at infinitely many powers.

+Dear Editors,
+
+We submit "Prime support and multiple-context-free languages in recurrent
+numeration" for consideration as an Original Research Article in Monatshefte
+fuer Mathematik.
+
+The article studies prime-support obstructions for canonical languages in
+eventually recurrent numeration systems. Its main results combine weak
+multiple-context-free pumping with the affine recurrence action, adic
+topology, and recurrence arithmetic. The manuscript is mathematically
+self-contained; none of its theorem proofs depends on a numbered result in
+the Supplementary Information.
+
+The submission includes two referee-facing online resources. Online Resource
+1 is the separately compiled Supplementary Information PDF containing the
+independent finite-state, Zeckendorf, and analytic comparisons described in
+the article. Online Resource 2 is the reproducibility archive containing the
+Python verifier, its unit tests, archived verifier and test outputs, the
+literature audit, checksums, and reproduction instructions. We ask that both
+online resources be made available to the referees with the main manuscript.
+
+The manuscript is not under consideration elsewhere. All authors have
+approved the submission. The authors declare no competing interests. No
+research datasets were generated or analysed.
+
+Sincerely,
+
+Haobo Ma
+AELF PTE LTD.
+auric@aelf.io
+
+Wenlin Zhang
+National University of Singapore
+e1327962@u.nus.edu

+## Current priority boundary (15 August 2026)
+
+The current manuscript uses the following narrower priority narrative, which
+supersedes any broader wording in earlier audit notes:
+
+- Ostrowski (1968) treats the linear multiplicative equation
+  `Phi(phi(z)) = g(z) Phi(z)` for rational data.
+- Nishioka (1985) directly implies that an algebraic solution of
+  `F(z^2) = H(z)^(-1) F(z)^2` is rational, by the one-variable specialization

+  prior work and is not a contribution of the paper.

+  collision lifting, effective rational-coboundary bounds and reconstruction,
+  and the cross-base elementary-two-group result.
+

+algebraic-solution rationality theorem, for the fixed-label Euler coordinate,
+for Frobenius-class products or equidistribution, or for the general
+periodic-data dictionary. This boundary matches the introduction and
+conclusion of the present manuscript.

-The paper determines the finite-state constant in Frobenius-class Mertens
-products. Its central point is that the product repeats the scalar orbit
-weight while keeping the primitive Frobenius label fixed. The relevant
-coordinate is therefore the fixed-label Euler transform F_rho, recovered from
-twisted determinants by Adams--Mobius inversion, rather than the periodic
-Artin logarithm L_rho, which powers the label under repetition.
+The paper proves finite radial determination for elementary two-group
+extensions over primitive edge shifts, allowing the two base shifts to be
+different. The number of radial locations is independent of the group rank.
+The inverse step combines determinant parity with Mahler special-value
+theorems, effective rational-coboundary bounds, and finite Pade
+reconstruction. The paper also gives an exact boundary collision and locates
+the obstruction to extending the finite bound to arbitrary finite groups.
 
-The manuscript states two independent corrections to Mohamed and Noorani's
-1999 Frobenius-class product theorem. Mixing of the base alone does not imply
-uniform Frobenius density; an extension-level transitivity/aperiodicity
-hypothesis, imposed here as a strict twisted gap, is required for the exponent
-|C|/|G|. Under that hypothesis, the proof also requires replacement of the
-Artin coordinate by F_rho. A trivial C_2-cocycle disproves the exponent under
-base mixing alone, and an exact strict-gap S_3 extension disproves the
-uncorrected Artin constant.

+multiplicative equation, and Nishioka's 1985 theorem directly supplies
+algebraic-solution rationality for the squared functional equation used here.
+The claimed increment is parity-compatible algebraic collision lifting,

+elementary-two-group theorem.

+## Abstract
 
-Let X_Gamma^+ be a mixing one-sided edge shift, let G be finite, and let a
-one-step cocycle label each primitive orbit gamma by a conjugacy class
-[g_gamma]. We determine the constant in the Frobenius-class Mertens product
-by separating the periodic Artin logarithm from the fixed-label Euler
-transform. The former powers the primitive label under repetition, whereas
-the latter repeats the scalar weight while keeping the primitive label fixed.
-Under the strict twisted spectral gap, we prove an Adams--Mobius determinant
-formula for F_rho(lambda^{-1}) and hence for every class-product constant.
-This gives two corrections to the theorem of Mohamed and Noorani (1999).
-Mixing of the base alone does not imply uniform Frobenius density, so an
-extension-level transitivity/aperiodicity condition, imposed here as the
-strict twisted gap, is required for the exponent |C|/|G|. Under this
-hypothesis, their constant also replaces chi_rho(g_gamma) by
-chi_rho(g_gamma^r) in the r-th logarithmic term. A trivial C_2-cocycle
-exhibits the first defect, while a strict-gap S_3 extension exhibits the
-second: its sign Artin logarithm vanishes although its fixed-label coordinate
-is strictly negative. We also give the corrected union-of-classes constant
-for the homogeneous-extension consequence.
+Let E=(C2)^r, and let two one-step E-cocycles lie over primitive edge shifts
+whose vertex counts are at most V; the base shifts need not be the same. For
+the primitive length-element counts p_(n,g), put E_g(y)=sum_(n>=1)
+p_(n,g) log(1-y^n). Without a twisted-gap hypothesis, equality of every
+element profile at 2V ceil(log_2(4V)) distinct radii in the common open Perron
+interval forces equality of every p_(n,g), provided that one sampled radius
+is algebraic. Thus the number of radial locations is independent of r,
+although each location supplies the full 2^r-component profile vector. For a
+reduced binary character-determinant ratio of total degree D>0, one algebraic
+collision identifies the complete real collision set, which has at most
+D ceil(log_2(2D))-1 points. The inverse mechanism is arithmetic: determinant
+parity, Nishioka's special-value theorem, and Nishioka's algebraic-solution
+rationality theorem force a normalized rational Mahler coboundary. A divisor
+l1 estimate gives an O(D log D) degree bound and one finite Pade system
+reconstructs or rejects the certificate. An exact four-vertex pair shows that
+one centered Perron-boundary profile vector does not suffice. For general
+finite groups, recovery holds from a radial set with an interior accumulation
+point; already for C3, Adams--Mobius inversion exhibits the obstruction to a
+finite bound by coupling determinant logarithms at infinitely many powers.

+Dear Editors,
+
+We submit "Prime support and multiple-context-free languages in recurrent
+numeration" for consideration as an Original Research Article in Monatshefte
+fuer Mathematik.
+
+The article studies prime-support obstructions for canonical languages in
+eventually recurrent numeration systems. Its main results combine weak
+multiple-context-free pumping with the affine recurrence action, adic
+topology, and recurrence arithmetic. The manuscript is mathematically
+self-contained; none of its theorem proofs depends on a numbered result in
+the Supplementary Information.
+
+The submission includes two referee-facing online resources. Online Resource
+1 is the separately compiled Supplementary Information PDF containing the
+independent finite-state, Zeckendorf, and analytic comparisons described in
+the article. Online Resource 2 is the reproducibility archive containing the
+Python verifier, its unit tests, archived verifier and test outputs, the
+literature audit, checksums, and reproduction instructions. We ask that both
+online resources be made available to the referees with the main manuscript.
+
+The manuscript is not under consideration elsewhere. All authors have
+approved the submission. The authors declare no competing interests. No
+research datasets were generated or analysed.
+
+Sincerely,
+
+Haobo Ma
+AELF PTE LTD.
+auric@aelf.io
+
+Wenlin Zhang
+National University of Singapore
+e1327962@u.nus.edu

+## Current priority boundary (15 August 2026)
+
+The current manuscript uses the following narrower priority narrative, which
+supersedes any broader wording in earlier audit notes:
+
+- Ostrowski (1968) treats the linear multiplicative equation
+  `Phi(phi(z)) = g(z) Phi(z)` for rational data.
+- Nishioka (1985) directly implies that an algebraic solution of
+  `F(z^2) = H(z)^(-1) F(z)^2` is rational, by the one-variable specialization
+  with `p = 2` and `R(z,Y) = Y^2/H(z)`. This algebraic-to-rational step is
+  prior work and is not a contribution of the paper.
+- The paper's claimed contribution is limited to parity-compatible algebraic
+  collision lifting, effective rational-coboundary bounds and reconstruction,
+  and the cross-base elementary-two-group result.
+
+In particular, the paper does not claim originality for the general
+algebraic-solution rationality theorem, for the fixed-label Euler coordinate,
+for Frobenius-class products or equidistribution, or for the general
+periodic-data dictionary. This boundary matches the introduction and
+conclusion of the present manuscript.

 Dear Editors,
 
-We submit the substantially refocused manuscript "Adams-corrected

+We submit "Finite radial determination of Frobenius profiles for elementary
+two-group extensions of shifts of finite type" for consideration as a
+Research Article in Ergodic Theory and Dynamical Systems.
 
-The paper determines the finite-state constant in Frobenius-class Mertens
-products. Its central point is that the product repeats the scalar orbit
-weight while keeping the primitive Frobenius label fixed. The relevant
-coordinate is therefore the fixed-label Euler transform F_rho, recovered from
-twisted determinants by Adams--Mobius inversion, rather than the periodic
-Artin logarithm L_rho, which powers the label under repetition.
+The paper proves finite radial determination for elementary two-group
+extensions over primitive edge shifts, allowing the two base shifts to be
+different. The number of radial locations is independent of the group rank.
+The inverse step combines determinant parity with Mahler special-value
+theorems, effective rational-coboundary bounds, and finite Pade
+reconstruction. The paper also gives an exact boundary collision and locates
+the obstruction to extending the finite bound to arbitrary finite groups.
 
-The manuscript states two independent corrections to Mohamed and Noorani's
-1999 Frobenius-class product theorem. Mixing of the base alone does not imply
-uniform Frobenius density; an extension-level transitivity/aperiodicity
-hypothesis, imposed here as a strict twisted gap, is required for the exponent
-|C|/|G|. Under that hypothesis, the proof also requires replacement of the
-Artin coordinate by F_rho. A trivial C_2-cocycle disproves the exponent under
-base mixing alone, and an exact strict-gap S_3 extension disproves the
-uncorrected Artin constant.
+The priority claim is deliberately narrow. Ostrowski treats the linear
+multiplicative equation, and Nishioka's 1985 theorem directly supplies
+algebraic-solution rationality for the squared functional equation used here.
+The claimed increment is parity-compatible algebraic collision lifting,
+effective rational-coboundary bounds and reconstruction, and the cross-base
+elementary-two-group theorem.

+## Abstract
 
-Let X_Gamma^+ be a mixing one-sided edge shift, let G be finite, and let a
-one-step cocycle label each primitive orbit gamma by a conjugacy class
-[g_gamma]. We determine the constant in the Frobenius-class Mertens product
-by separating the periodic Artin logarithm from the fixed-label Euler
-transform. The former powers the primitive label under repetition, whereas
-the latter repeats the scalar weight while keeping the primitive label fixed.
-Under the strict twisted spectral gap, we prove an Adams--Mobius determinant
-formula for F_rho(lambda^{-1}) and hence for every class-product constant.
-This gives two corrections to the theorem of Mohamed and Noorani (1999).
-Mixing of the base alone does not imply uniform Frobenius density, so an
-extension-level transitivity/aperiodicity condition, imposed here as the
-strict twisted gap, is required for the exponent |C|/|G|. Under this
-hypothesis, their constant also replaces chi_rho(g_gamma) by
-chi_rho(g_gamma^r) in the r-th logarithmic term. A trivial C_2-cocycle
-exhibits the first defect, while a strict-gap S_3 extension exhibits the
-second: its sign Artin logarithm vanishes although its fixed-label coordinate
-is strictly negative. We also give the corrected union-of-classes constant
-for the homogeneous-extension consequence.
+Let E=(C2)^r, and let two one-step E-cocycles lie over primitive edge shifts
+whose vertex counts are at most V; the base shifts need not be the same. For
+the primitive length-element counts p_(n,g), put E_g(y)=sum_(n>=1)
+p_(n,g) log(1-y^n). Without a twisted-gap hypothesis, equality of every
+element profile at 2V ceil(log_2(4V)) distinct radii in the common open Perron
+interval forces equality of every p_(n,g), provided that one sampled radius
+is algebraic. Thus the number of radial locations is independent of r,
+although each location supplies the full 2^r-component profile vector. For a
+reduced binary character-determinant ratio of total degree D>0, one algebraic
+collision identifies the complete real collision set, which has at most
+D ceil(log_2(2D))-1 points. The inverse mechanism is arithmetic: determinant
+parity, Nishioka's special-value theorem, and Nishioka's algebraic-solution
+rationality theorem force a normalized rational Mahler coboundary. A divisor
+l1 estimate gives an O(D log D) degree bound and one finite Pade system
+reconstructs or rejects the certificate. An exact four-vertex pair shows that
+one centered Perron-boundary profile vector does not suffice. For general
+finite groups, recovery holds from a radial set with an interior accumulation
+point; already for C3, Adams--Mobius inversion exhibits the obstruction to a
+finite bound by coupling determinant logarithms at infinitely many powers.

+Dear Editors,
+
+We submit "Prime support and multiple-context-free languages in recurrent
+numeration" for consideration as an Original Research Article in Monatshefte
+fuer Mathematik.
+
+The article studies prime-support obstructions for canonical languages in
+eventually recurrent numeration systems. Its main results combine weak
+multiple-context-free pumping with the affine recurrence action, adic
+topology, and recurrence arithmetic. The manuscript is mathematically
+self-contained; none of its theorem proofs depends on a numbered result in
+the Supplementary Information.
+
+The submission includes two referee-facing online resources. Online Resource
+1 is the separately compiled Supplementary Information PDF containing the
+independent finite-state, Zeckendorf, and analytic comparisons described in
+the article. Online Resource 2 is the reproducibility archive containing the
+Python verifier, its unit tests, archived verifier and test outputs, the
+literature audit, checksums, and reproduction instructions. We ask that both
+online resources be made available to the referees with the main manuscript.
+
+The manuscript is not under consideration elsewhere. All authors have
+approved the submission. The authors declare no competing interests. No
+research datasets were generated or analysed.
+
+Sincerely,
+
+Haobo Ma
+AELF PTE LTD.
+auric@aelf.io
+
+Wenlin Zhang
+National University of Singapore
+e1327962@u.nus.edu

+Let E=(C2)^r, and let two one-step E-cocycles lie over primitive edge shifts
+whose vertex counts are at most V; the base shifts need not be the same. For
+the primitive length-element counts p_(n,g), put E_g(y)=sum_(n>=1)
+p_(n,g) log(1-y^n). Without a twisted-gap hypothesis, equality of every
+element profile at 2V ceil(log_2(4V)) distinct radii in the common open Perron
+interval forces equality of every p_(n,g), provided that one sampled radius
+is algebraic. Thus the number of radial locations is independent of r,
+although each location supplies the full 2^r-component profile vector. For a
+reduced binary character-determinant ratio of total degree D>0, one algebraic
+collision identifies the complete real collision set, which has at most
+D ceil(log_2(2D))-1 points. The inverse mechanism is arithmetic: determinant
+parity, Nishioka's special-value theorem, and Nishioka's algebraic-solution
+rationality theorem force a normalized rational Mahler coboundary. A divisor
+l1 estimate gives an O(D log D) degree bound and one finite Pade system
+reconstructs or rejects the certificate. An exact four-vertex pair shows that
+one centered Perron-boundary profile vector does not suffice. For general
+finite groups, recovery holds from a radial set with an interior accumulation
+point; already for C3, Adams--Mobius inversion exhibits the obstruction to a
+finite bound by coupling determinant logarithms at infinitely many powers.

+Dear Editors,
+
+We submit "Prime support and multiple-context-free languages in recurrent
+numeration" for consideration as an Original Research Article in Monatshefte
+fuer Mathematik.
+
+The article studies prime-support obstructions for canonical languages in
+eventually recurrent numeration systems. Its main results combine weak
+multiple-context-free pumping with the affine recurrence action, adic
+topology, and recurrence arithmetic. The manuscript is mathematically
+self-contained; none of its theorem proofs depends on a numbered result in
+the Supplementary Information.
+
+The submission includes two referee-facing online resources. Online Resource
+1 is the separately compiled Supplementary Information PDF containing the
+independent finite-state, Zeckendorf, and analytic comparisons described in
+the article. Online Resource 2 is the reproducibility archive containing the
+Python verifier, its unit tests, archived verifier and test outputs, the
+literature audit, checksums, and reproduction instructions. We ask that both
+online resources be made available to the referees with the main manuscript.

+## Abstract
 
-Let X_Gamma^+ be a mixing one-sided edge shift, let G be finite, and let a
-one-step cocycle label each primitive orbit gamma by a conjugacy class
-[g_gamma]. We determine the constant in the Frobenius-class Mertens product

-the latter repeats the scalar weight while keeping the primitive label fixed.
-Under the strict twisted spectral gap, we prove an Adams--Mobius determinant
-formula for F_rho(lambda^{-1}) and hence for every class-product constant.
-This gives two corrections to the theorem of Mohamed and Noorani (1999).

+Let E=(C2)^r, and let two one-step E-cocycles lie over primitive edge shifts
+whose vertex counts are at most V; the base shifts need not be the same. For
+the primitive length-element counts p_(n,g), put E_g(y)=sum_(n>=1)
+p_(n,g) log(1-y^n). Without a twisted-gap hypothesis, equality of every
+element profile at 2V ceil(log_2(4V)) distinct radii in the common open Perron
+interval forces equality of every p_(n,g), provided that one sampled radius
+is algebraic. Thus the number of radial locations is independent of r,
+although each location supplies the full 2^r-component profile vector. For a
+reduced binary character-determinant ratio of total degree D>0, one algebraic
+collision identifies the complete real collision set, which has at most
+D ceil(log_2(2D))-1 points. The inverse mechanism is arithmetic: determinant
+parity, Nishioka's special-value theorem, and Nishioka's algebraic-solution
+rationality theorem force a normalized rational Mahler coboundary. A divisor
+l1 estimate gives an O(D log D) degree bound and one finite Pade system
+reconstructs or rejects the certificate. An exact four-vertex pair shows that
+one centered Perron-boundary profile vector does not suffice. For general
+finite groups, recovery holds from a radial set with an interior accumulation
+point; already for C3, Adams--Mobius inversion exhibits the obstruction to a
+finite bound by coupling determinant logarithms at infinitely many powers.

+Dear Editors,
+
+We submit "Prime support and multiple-context-free languages in recurrent
+numeration" for consideration as an Original Research Article in Monatshefte
+fuer Mathematik.
+
+The article studies prime-support obstructions for canonical languages in
+eventually recurrent numeration systems. Its main results combine weak
+multiple-context-free pumping with the affine recurrence action, adic
+topology, and recurrence arithmetic. The manuscript is mathematically
+self-contained; none of its theorem proofs depends on a numbered result in
+the Supplementary Information.
+
+The submission includes two referee-facing online resources. Online Resource
+1 is the separately compiled Supplementary Information PDF containing the
+independent finite-state, Zeckendorf, and analytic comparisons described in
+the article. Online Resource 2 is the reproducibility archive containing the
+Python verifier, its unit tests, archived verifier and test outputs, the
+literature audit, checksums, and reproduction instructions. We ask that both
+online resources be made available to the referees with the main manuscript.
+
+The manuscript is not under consideration elsewhere. All authors have
+approved the submission. The authors declare no competing interests. No
+research datasets were generated or analysed.
+

+
+Haobo Ma
+AELF PTE LTD.
+auric@aelf.io
+
+Wenlin Zhang

+Dear Editors,
+
+We submit "Prime support and multiple-context-free languages in recurrent
+numeration" for consideration as an Original Research Article in Monatshefte
+fuer Mathematik.
+
+The article studies prime-support obstructions for canonical languages in
+eventually recurrent numeration systems. Its main results combine weak
+multiple-context-free pumping with the affine recurrence action, adic
+topology, and recurrence arithmetic. The manuscript is mathematically
+self-contained; none of its theorem proofs depends on a numbered result in
+the Supplementary Information.
+
+The submission includes two referee-facing online resources. Online Resource
+1 is the separately compiled Supplementary Information PDF containing the
+independent finite-state, Zeckendorf, and analytic comparisons described in

+## Abstract
 
-Let X_Gamma^+ be a mixing one-sided edge shift, let G be finite, and let a
-one-step cocycle label each primitive orbit gamma by a conjugacy class
-[g_gamma]. We determine the constant in the Frobenius-class Mertens product
-by separating the periodic Artin logarithm from the fixed-label Euler

-the latter repeats the scalar weight while keeping the primitive label fixed.
-Under the strict twisted spectral gap, we prove an Adams--Mobius determinant
-formula for F_rho(lambda^{-1}) and hence for every class-product constant.
-This gives two corrections to the theorem of Mohamed and Noorani (1999).
-Mixing of the base alone does not imply uniform Frobenius density, so an
-extension-level transitivity/aperiodicity condition, imposed here as the
-strict twisted gap, is required for the exponent |C|/|G|. Under this
-hypothesis, their constant also replaces chi_rho(g_gamma) by
-chi_rho(g_gamma^r) in the r-th logarithmic term. A trivial C_2-cocycle
-exhibits the first defect, while a strict-gap S_3 extension exhibits the

+Let E=(C2)^r, and let two one-step E-cocycles lie over primitive edge shifts
+whose vertex counts are at most V; the base shifts need not be the same. For
+the primitive length-element counts p_(n,g), put E_g(y)=sum_(n>=1)
+p_(n,g) log(1-y^n). Without a twisted-gap hypothesis, equality of every
+element profile at 2V ceil(log_2(4V)) distinct radii in the common open Perron
+interval forces equality of every p_(n,g), provided that one sampled radius
+is algebraic. Thus the number of radial locations is independent of r,
+although each location supplies the full 2^r-component profile vector. For a
+reduced binary character-determinant ratio of total degree D>0, one algebraic
+collision identifies the complete real collision set, which has at most
+D ceil(log_2(2D))-1 points. The inverse mechanism is arithmetic: determinant
+parity, Nishioka's special-value theorem, and Nishioka's algebraic-solution
+rationality theorem force a normalized rational Mahler coboundary. A divisor
+l1 estimate gives an O(D log D) degree bound and one finite Pade system
+reconstructs or rejects the certificate. An exact four-vertex pair shows that
+one centered Perron-boundary profile vector does not suffice. For general
+finite groups, recovery holds from a radial set with an interior accumulation
+point; already for C3, Adams--Mobius inversion exhibits the obstruction to a
+finite bound by coupling determinant logarithms at infinitely many powers.

+Dear Editors,
+
+We submit "Prime support and multiple-context-free languages in recurrent
+numeration" for consideration as an Original Research Article in Monatshefte
+fuer Mathematik.
+
+The article studies prime-support obstructions for canonical languages in
+eventually recurrent numeration systems. Its main results combine weak
+multiple-context-free pumping with the affine recurrence action, adic
+topology, and recurrence arithmetic. The manuscript is mathematically
+self-contained; none of its theorem proofs depends on a numbered result in
+the Supplementary Information.
+
+The submission includes two referee-facing online resources. Online Resource
+1 is the separately compiled Supplementary Information PDF containing the
+independent finite-state, Zeckendorf, and analytic comparisons described in
+the article. Online Resource 2 is the reproducibility archive containing the
+Python verifier, its unit tests, archived verifier and test outputs, the
+literature audit, checksums, and reproduction instructions. We ask that both
+online resources be made available to the referees with the main manuscript.
+
+The manuscript is not under consideration elsewhere. All authors have
+approved the submission. The authors declare no competing interests. No
+research datasets were generated or analysed.

+## Current priority boundary (15 August 2026)
+
+The current manuscript uses the following narrower priority narrative, which
+supersedes any broader wording in earlier audit notes:
+
+- Ostrowski (1968) treats the linear multiplicative equation
+  `Phi(phi(z)) = g(z) Phi(z)` for rational data.
+- Nishioka (1985) directly implies that an algebraic solution of
+  `F(z^2) = H(z)^(-1) F(z)^2` is rational, by the one-variable specialization
+  with `p = 2` and `R(z,Y) = Y^2/H(z)`. This algebraic-to-rational step is
+  prior work and is not a contribution of the paper.
+- The paper's claimed contribution is limited to parity-compatible algebraic
+  collision lifting, effective rational-coboundary bounds and reconstruction,
+  and the cross-base elementary-two-group result.
+
+In particular, the paper does not claim originality for the general
+algebraic-solution rationality theorem, for the fixed-label Euler coordinate,
+for Frobenius-class products or equidistribution, or for the general
+periodic-data dictionary. This boundary matches the introduction and
+conclusion of the present manuscript.

 Dear Editors,
 
-We submit the substantially refocused manuscript "Adams-corrected

+We submit "Finite radial determination of Frobenius profiles for elementary
+two-group extensions of shifts of finite type" for consideration as a
+Research Article in Ergodic Theory and Dynamical Systems.
 
-The paper determines the finite-state constant in Frobenius-class Mertens
-products. Its central point is that the product repeats the scalar orbit
-weight while keeping the primitive Frobenius label fixed. The relevant
-coordinate is therefore the fixed-label Euler transform F_rho, recovered from
-twisted determinants by Adams--Mobius inversion, rather than the periodic
-Artin logarithm L_rho, which powers the label under repetition.
+The paper proves finite radial determination for elementary two-group
+extensions over primitive edge shifts, allowing the two base shifts to be
+different. The number of radial locations is independent of the group rank.
+The inverse step combines determinant parity with Mahler special-value
+theorems, effective rational-coboundary bounds, and finite Pade
+reconstruction. The paper also gives an exact boundary collision and locates
+the obstruction to extending the finite bound to arbitrary finite groups.
 
-The manuscript states two independent corrections to Mohamed and Noorani's
-1999 Frobenius-class product theorem. Mixing of the base alone does not imply
-uniform Frobenius density; an extension-level transitivity/aperiodicity
-hypothesis, imposed here as a strict twisted gap, is required for the exponent
-|C|/|G|. Under that hypothesis, the proof also requires replacement of the
-Artin coordinate by F_rho. A trivial C_2-cocycle disproves the exponent under
-base mixing alone, and an exact strict-gap S_3 extension disproves the
-uncorrected Artin constant.
+The priority claim is deliberately narrow. Ostrowski treats the linear
+multiplicative equation, and Nishioka's 1985 theorem directly supplies
+algebraic-solution rationality for the squared functional equation used here.

+elementary-two-group theorem.

+## Abstract
 
-Let X_Gamma^+ be a mixing one-sided edge shift, let G be finite, and let a
-one-step cocycle label each primitive orbit gamma by a conjugacy class
-[g_gamma]. We determine the constant in the Frobenius-class Mertens product
-by separating the periodic Artin logarithm from the fixed-label Euler
-transform. The former powers the primitive label under repetition, whereas
-the latter repeats the scalar weight while keeping the primitive label fixed.
-Under the strict twisted spectral gap, we prove an Adams--Mobius determinant
-formula for F_rho(lambda^{-1}) and hence for every class-product constant.
-This gives two corrections to the theorem of Mohamed and Noorani (1999).
-Mixing of the base alone does not imply uniform Frobenius density, so an
-extension-level transitivity/aperiodicity condition, imposed here as the
-strict twisted gap, is required for the exponent |C|/|G|. Under this
-hypothesis, their constant also replaces chi_rho(g_gamma) by
-chi_rho(g_gamma^r) in the r-th logarithmic term. A trivial C_2-cocycle
-exhibits the first defect, while a strict-gap S_3 extension exhibits the
-second: its sign Artin logarithm vanishes although its fixed-label coordinate
-is strictly negative. We also give the corrected union-of-classes constant
-for the homogeneous-extension consequence.
+Let E=(C2)^r, and let two one-step E-cocycles lie over primitive edge shifts
+whose vertex counts are at most V; the base shifts need not be the same. For
+the primitive length-element counts p_(n,g), put E_g(y)=sum_(n>=1)
+p_(n,g) log(1-y^n). Without a twisted-gap hypothesis, equality of every
+element profile at 2V ceil(log_2(4V)) distinct radii in the common open Perron
+interval forces equality of every p_(n,g), provided that one sampled radius
+is algebraic. Thus the number of radial locations is independent of r,
+although each location supplies the full 2^r-component profile vector. For a
+reduced binary character-determinant ratio of total degree D>0, one algebraic
+collision identifies the complete real collision set, which has at most
+D ceil(log_2(2D))-1 points. The inverse mechanism is arithmetic: determinant
+parity, Nishioka's special-value theorem, and Nishioka's algebraic-solution
+rationality theorem force a normalized rational Mahler coboundary. A divisor
+l1 estimate gives an O(D log D) degree bound and one finite Pade system
+reconstructs or rejects the certificate. An exact four-vertex pair shows that
+one centered Perron-boundary profile vector does not suffice. For general
+finite groups, recovery holds from a radial set with an interior accumulation
+point; already for C3, Adams--Mobius inversion exhibits the obstruction to a
+finite bound by coupling determinant logarithms at infinitely many powers.

+Dear Editors,
+
+We submit "Prime support and multiple-context-free languages in recurrent
+numeration" for consideration as an Original Research Article in Monatshefte
+fuer Mathematik.
+
+The article studies prime-support obstructions for canonical languages in
+eventually recurrent numeration systems. Its main results combine weak
+multiple-context-free pumping with the affine recurrence action, adic
+topology, and recurrence arithmetic. The manuscript is mathematically
+self-contained; none of its theorem proofs depends on a numbered result in
+the Supplementary Information.
+
+The submission includes two referee-facing online resources. Online Resource
+1 is the separately compiled Supplementary Information PDF containing the
+independent finite-state, Zeckendorf, and analytic comparisons described in
+the article. Online Resource 2 is the reproducibility archive containing the
+Python verifier, its unit tests, archived verifier and test outputs, the
+literature audit, checksums, and reproduction instructions. We ask that both
+online resources be made available to the referees with the main manuscript.
+
+The manuscript is not under consideration elsewhere. All authors have
+approved the submission. The authors declare no competing interests. No
+research datasets were generated or analysed.
+
+Sincerely,
+
+Haobo Ma
+AELF PTE LTD.
+auric@aelf.io
+
+Wenlin Zhang
+National University of Singapore
+e1327962@u.nus.edu

+Let E=(C2)^r, and let two one-step E-cocycles lie over primitive edge shifts
+whose vertex counts are at most V; the base shifts need not be the same. For
+the primitive length-element counts p_(n,g), put E_g(y)=sum_(n>=1)
+p_(n,g) log(1-y^n). Without a twisted-gap hypothesis, equality of every
+element profile at 2V ceil(log_2(4V)) distinct radii in the common open Perron

+is algebraic. Thus the number of radial locations is independent of r,
+although each location supplies the full 2^r-component profile vector. For a
+reduced binary character-determinant ratio of total degree D>0, one algebraic
+collision identifies the complete real collision set, which has at most
+D ceil(log_2(2D))-1 points. The inverse mechanism is arithmetic: determinant
+parity, Nishioka's special-value theorem, and Nishioka's algebraic-solution

+l1 estimate gives an O(D log D) degree bound and one finite Pade system
+reconstructs or rejects the certificate. An exact four-vertex pair shows that
+one centered Perron-boundary profile vector does not suffice. For general
+finite groups, recovery holds from a radial set with an interior accumulation
+point; already for C3, Adams--Mobius inversion exhibits the obstruction to a
+finite bound by coupling determinant logarithms at infinitely many powers.

+Dear Editors,
+
+We submit "Prime support and multiple-context-free languages in recurrent
+numeration" for consideration as an Original Research Article in Monatshefte
+fuer Mathematik.
+
+The article studies prime-support obstructions for canonical languages in
+eventually recurrent numeration systems. Its main results combine weak
+multiple-context-free pumping with the affine recurrence action, adic
+topology, and recurrence arithmetic. The manuscript is mathematically
+self-contained; none of its theorem proofs depends on a numbered result in
+the Supplementary Information.
+
+The submission includes two referee-facing online resources. Online Resource
+1 is the separately compiled Supplementary Information PDF containing the
+independent finite-state, Zeckendorf, and analytic comparisons described in
+the article. Online Resource 2 is the reproducibility archive containing the
+Python verifier, its unit tests, archived verifier and test outputs, the
+literature audit, checksums, and reproduction instructions. We ask that both
+online resources be made available to the referees with the main manuscript.

+## Current priority boundary (15 August 2026)
+
+The current manuscript uses the following narrower priority narrative, which
+supersedes any broader wording in earlier audit notes:
+
+- Ostrowski (1968) treats the linear multiplicative equation
+  `Phi(phi(z)) = g(z) Phi(z)` for rational data.
+- Nishioka (1985) directly implies that an algebraic solution of
+  `F(z^2) = H(z)^(-1) F(z)^2` is rational, by the one-variable specialization
+  with `p = 2` and `R(z,Y) = Y^2/H(z)`. This algebraic-to-rational step is
+  prior work and is not a contribution of the paper.
+- The paper's claimed contribution is limited to parity-compatible algebraic
+  collision lifting, effective rational-coboundary bounds and reconstruction,
+  and the cross-base elementary-two-group result.
+
+In particular, the paper does not claim originality for the general
+algebraic-solution rationality theorem, for the fixed-label Euler coordinate,
+for Frobenius-class products or equidistribution, or for the general
+periodic-data dictionary. This boundary matches the introduction and
+conclusion of the present manuscript.

 Dear Editors,
 
-We submit the substantially refocused manuscript "Adams-corrected

-The paper determines the finite-state constant in Frobenius-class Mertens
-products. Its central point is that the product repeats the scalar orbit
-weight while keeping the primitive Frobenius label fixed. The relevant
-coordinate is therefore the fixed-label Euler transform F_rho, recovered from
-twisted determinants by Adams--Mobius inversion, rather than the periodic
-Artin logarithm L_rho, which powers the label under repetition.
+The paper proves finite radial determination for elementary two-group
+extensions over primitive edge shifts, allowing the two base shifts to be
+different. The number of radial locations is independent of the group rank.
+The inverse step combines determinant parity with Mahler special-value
+theorems, effective rational-coboundary bounds, and finite Pade
+reconstruction. The paper also gives an exact boundary collision and locates
+the obstruction to extending the finite bound to arbitrary finite groups.
 
-The manuscript states two independent corrections to Mohamed and Noorani's
-1999 Frobenius-class product theorem. Mixing of the base alone does not imply
-uniform Frobenius density; an extension-level transitivity/aperiodicity
-hypothesis, imposed here as a strict twisted gap, is required for the exponent
-|C|/|G|. Under that hypothesis, the proof also requires replacement of the
-Artin coordinate by F_rho. A trivial C_2-cocycle disproves the exponent under
-base mixing alone, and an exact strict-gap S_3 extension disproves the
-uncorrected Artin constant.
+The priority claim is deliberately narrow. Ostrowski treats the linear
+multiplicative equation, and Nishioka's 1985 theorem directly supplies
+algebraic-solution rationality for the squared functional equation used here.
+The claimed increment is parity-compatible algebraic collision lifting,
+effective rational-coboundary bounds and reconstruction, and the cross-base
+elementary-two-group theorem.

+## Abstract
 
-Let X_Gamma^+ be a mixing one-sided edge shift, let G be finite, and let a
-one-step cocycle label each primitive orbit gamma by a conjugacy class
-[g_gamma]. We determine the constant in the Frobenius-class Mertens product
-by separating the periodic Artin logarithm from the fixed-label Euler
-transform. The former powers the primitive label under repetition, whereas
-the latter repeats the scalar weight while keeping the primitive label fixed.
-Under the strict twisted spectral gap, we prove an Adams--Mobius determinant
-formula for F_rho(lambda^{-1}) and hence for every class-product constant.
-This gives two corrections to the theorem of Mohamed and Noorani (1999).
-Mixing of the base alone does not imply uniform Frobenius density, so an
-extension-level transitivity/aperiodicity condition, imposed here as the
-strict twisted gap, is required for the exponent |C|/|G|. Under this
-hypothesis, their constant also replaces chi_rho(g_gamma) by
-chi_rho(g_gamma^r) in the r-th logarithmic term. A trivial C_2-cocycle
-exhibits the first defect, while a strict-gap S_3 extension exhibits the
-second: its sign Artin logarithm vanishes although its fixed-label coordinate
-is strictly negative. We also give the corrected union-of-classes constant
-for the homogeneous-extension consequence.
+Let E=(C2)^r, and let two one-step E-cocycles lie over primitive edge shifts
+whose vertex counts are at most V; the base shifts need not be the same. For
+the primitive length-element counts p_(n,g), put E_g(y)=sum_(n>=1)
+p_(n,g) log(1-y^n). Without a twisted-gap hypothesis, equality of every
+element profile at 2V ceil(log_2(4V)) distinct radii in the common open Perron
+interval forces equality of every p_(n,g), provided that one sampled radius
+is algebraic. Thus the number of radial locations is independent of r,
+although each location supplies the full 2^r-component profile vector. For a
+reduced binary character-determinant ratio of total degree D>0, one algebraic
+collision identifies the complete real collision set, which has at most
+D ceil(log_2(2D))-1 points. The inverse mechanism is arithmetic: determinant
+parity, Nishioka's special-value theorem, and Nishioka's algebraic-solution
+rationality theorem force a normalized rational Mahler coboundary. A divisor
+l1 estimate gives an O(D log D) degree bound and one finite Pade system
+reconstructs or rejects the certificate. An exact four-vertex pair shows that
+one centered Perron-boundary profile vector does not suffice. For general
+finite groups, recovery holds from a radial set with an interior accumulation
+point; already for C3, Adams--Mobius inversion exhibits the obstruction to a
+finite bound by coupling determinant logarithms at infinitely many powers.

+Dear Editors,
+
+We submit "Prime support and multiple-context-free languages in recurrent
+numeration" for consideration as an Original Research Article in Monatshefte
+fuer Mathematik.
+
+The article studies prime-support obstructions for canonical languages in
+eventually recurrent numeration systems. Its main results combine weak
+multiple-context-free pumping with the affine recurrence action, adic
+topology, and recurrence arithmetic. The manuscript is mathematically
+self-contained; none of its theorem proofs depends on a numbered result in
+the Supplementary Information.
+
+The submission includes two referee-facing online resources. Online Resource
+1 is the separately compiled Supplementary Information PDF containing the
+independent finite-state, Zeckendorf, and analytic comparisons described in
+the article. Online Resource 2 is the reproducibility archive containing the
+Python verifier, its unit tests, archived verifier and test outputs, the
+literature audit, checksums, and reproduction instructions. We ask that both
+online resources be made available to the referees with the main manuscript.
+
+The manuscript is not under consideration elsewhere. All authors have
+approved the submission. The authors declare no competing interests. No
+research datasets were generated or analysed.

-This gives two corrections to the theorem of Mohamed and Noorani (1999).
-Mixing of the base alone does not imply uniform Frobenius density, so an

+Let E=(C2)^r, and let two one-step E-cocycles lie over primitive edge shifts
+whose vertex counts are at most V; the base shifts need not be the same. For
+the primitive length-element counts p_(n,g), put E_g(y)=sum_(n>=1)
+p_(n,g) log(1-y^n). Without a twisted-gap hypothesis, equality of every
+element profile at 2V ceil(log_2(4V)) distinct radii in the common open Perron
+interval forces equality of every p_(n,g), provided that one sampled radius
+is algebraic. Thus the number of radial locations is independent of r,
+although each location supplies the full 2^r-component profile vector. For a
+reduced binary character-determinant ratio of total degree D>0, one algebraic
+collision identifies the complete real collision set, which has at most
+D ceil(log_2(2D))-1 points. The inverse mechanism is arithmetic: determinant
+parity, Nishioka's special-value theorem, and Nishioka's algebraic-solution
+rationality theorem force a normalized rational Mahler coboundary. A divisor
+l1 estimate gives an O(D log D) degree bound and one finite Pade system
+reconstructs or rejects the certificate. An exact four-vertex pair shows that
+one centered Perron-boundary profile vector does not suffice. For general
+finite groups, recovery holds from a radial set with an interior accumulation
+point; already for C3, Adams--Mobius inversion exhibits the obstruction to a
+finite bound by coupling determinant logarithms at infinitely many powers.

+Dear Editors,
+
+We submit "Prime support and multiple-context-free languages in recurrent
+numeration" for consideration as an Original Research Article in Monatshefte
+fuer Mathematik.
+
+The article studies prime-support obstructions for canonical languages in
+eventually recurrent numeration systems. Its main results combine weak
+multiple-context-free pumping with the affine recurrence action, adic
+topology, and recurrence arithmetic. The manuscript is mathematically
+self-contained; none of its theorem proofs depends on a numbered result in
+the Supplementary Information.
+
+The submission includes two referee-facing online resources. Online Resource
+1 is the separately compiled Supplementary Information PDF containing the
+independent finite-state, Zeckendorf, and analytic comparisons described in
+the article. Online Resource 2 is the reproducibility archive containing the
+Python verifier, its unit tests, archived verifier and test outputs, the
+literature audit, checksums, and reproduction instructions. We ask that both
+online resources be made available to the referees with the main manuscript.
+
+The manuscript is not under consideration elsewhere. All authors have
+approved the submission. The authors declare no competing interests. No
+research datasets were generated or analysed.
+
+Sincerely,
+
+Haobo Ma
+AELF PTE LTD.
+auric@aelf.io
+
+Wenlin Zhang
+National University of Singapore

+## Abstract
 
-Let X_Gamma^+ be a mixing one-sided edge shift, let G be finite, and let a
-one-step cocycle label each primitive orbit gamma by a conjugacy class
-[g_gamma]. We determine the constant in the Frobenius-class Mertens product
-by separating the periodic Artin logarithm from the fixed-label Euler
-transform. The former powers the primitive label under repetition, whereas
-the latter repeats the scalar weight while keeping the primitive label fixed.
-Under the strict twisted spectral gap, we prove an Adams--Mobius determinant
-formula for F_rho(lambda^{-1}) and hence for every class-product constant.
-This gives two corrections to the theorem of Mohamed and Noorani (1999).
-Mixing of the base alone does not imply uniform Frobenius density, so an
-extension-level transitivity/aperiodicity condition, imposed here as the
-strict twisted gap, is required for the exponent |C|/|G|. Under this
-hypothesis, their constant also replaces chi_rho(g_gamma) by
-chi_rho(g_gamma^r) in the r-th logarithmic term. A trivial C_2-cocycle
-exhibits the first defect, while a strict-gap S_3 extension exhibits the
-second: its sign Artin logarithm vanishes although its fixed-label coordinate
-is strictly negative. We also give the corrected union-of-classes constant
-for the homogeneous-extension consequence.
+Let E=(C2)^r, and let two one-step E-cocycles lie over primitive edge shifts
+whose vertex counts are at most V; the base shifts need not be the same. For
+the primitive length-element counts p_(n,g), put E_g(y)=sum_(n>=1)
+p_(n,g) log(1-y^n). Without a twisted-gap hypothesis, equality of every
+element profile at 2V ceil(log_2(4V)) distinct radii in the common open Perron
+interval forces equality of every p_(n,g), provided that one sampled radius
+is algebraic. Thus the number of radial locations is independent of r,
+although each location supplies the full 2^r-component profile vector. For a
+reduced binary character-determinant ratio of total degree D>0, one algebraic
+collision identifies the complete real collision set, which has at most
+D ceil(log_2(2D))-1 points. The inverse mechanism is arithmetic: determinant
+parity, Nishioka's special-value theorem, and Nishioka's algebraic-solution
+rationality theorem force a normalized rational Mahler coboundary. A divisor
+l1 estimate gives an O(D log D) degree bound and one finite Pade system
+reconstructs or rejects the certificate. An exact four-vertex pair shows that
+one centered Perron-boundary profile vector does not suffice. For general
+finite groups, recovery holds from a radial set with an interior accumulation
+point; already for C3, Adams--Mobius inversion exhibits the obstruction to a
+finite bound by coupling determinant logarithms at infinitely many powers.

+## Current priority boundary (15 August 2026)

+The current manuscript uses the following narrower priority narrative, which
+supersedes any broader wording in earlier audit notes:
+
+- Ostrowski (1968) treats the linear multiplicative equation
+  `Phi(phi(z)) = g(z) Phi(z)` for rational data.

-This gives two corrections to the theorem of Mohamed and Noorani (1999).

+Let E=(C2)^r, and let two one-step E-cocycles lie over primitive edge shifts
+whose vertex counts are at most V; the base shifts need not be the same. For
+the primitive length-element counts p_(n,g), put E_g(y)=sum_(n>=1)
+p_(n,g) log(1-y^n). Without a twisted-gap hypothesis, equality of every
+element profile at 2V ceil(log_2(4V)) distinct radii in the common open Perron
+interval forces equality of every p_(n,g), provided that one sampled radius
+is algebraic. Thus the number of radial locations is independent of r,
+although each location supplies the full 2^r-component profile vector. For a
+reduced binary character-determinant ratio of total degree D>0, one algebraic
+collision identifies the complete real collision set, which has at most
+D ceil(log_2(2D))-1 points. The inverse mechanism is arithmetic: determinant
+parity, Nishioka's special-value theorem, and Nishioka's algebraic-solution
+rationality theorem force a normalized rational Mahler coboundary. A divisor
+l1 estimate gives an O(D log D) degree bound and one finite Pade system
+reconstructs or rejects the certificate. An exact four-vertex pair shows that
+one centered Perron-boundary profile vector does not suffice. For general
+finite groups, recovery holds from a radial set with an interior accumulation
+point; already for C3, Adams--Mobius inversion exhibits the obstruction to a
+finite bound by coupling determinant logarithms at infinitely many powers.

+Dear Editors,
+
+We submit "Prime support and multiple-context-free languages in recurrent
+numeration" for consideration as an Original Research Article in Monatshefte
+fuer Mathematik.
+
+The article studies prime-support obstructions for canonical languages in
+eventually recurrent numeration systems. Its main results combine weak
+multiple-context-free pumping with the affine recurrence action, adic
+topology, and recurrence arithmetic. The manuscript is mathematically
+self-contained; none of its theorem proofs depends on a numbered result in
+the Supplementary Information.
+
+The submission includes two referee-facing online resources. Online Resource
+1 is the separately compiled Supplementary Information PDF containing the
+independent finite-state, Zeckendorf, and analytic comparisons described in
+the article. Online Resource 2 is the reproducibility archive containing the
+Python verifier, its unit tests, archived verifier and test outputs, the
+literature audit, checksums, and reproduction instructions. We ask that both
+online resources be made available to the referees with the main manuscript.
+
+The manuscript is not under consideration elsewhere. All authors have
+approved the submission. The authors declare no competing interests. No
+research datasets were generated or analysed.
+
+Sincerely,
+
+Haobo Ma
+AELF PTE LTD.
+auric@aelf.io
+
+Wenlin Zhang
+National University of Singapore
+e1327962@u.nus.edu

+Dear Editors,
+
+We submit "Prime support and multiple-context-free languages in recurrent
+numeration" for consideration as an Original Research Article in Monatshefte
+fuer Mathematik.
+
+The article studies prime-support obstructions for canonical languages in
+eventually recurrent numeration systems. Its main results combine weak
+multiple-context-free pumping with the affine recurrence action, adic
+topology, and recurrence arithmetic. The manuscript is mathematically
+self-contained; none of its theorem proofs depends on a numbered result in
+the Supplementary Information.
+
+The submission includes two referee-facing online resources. Online Resource
+1 is the separately compiled Supplementary Information PDF containing the
+independent finite-state, Zeckendorf, and analytic comparisons described in
+the article. Online Resource 2 is the reproducibility archive containing the
+Python verifier, its unit tests, archived verifier and test outputs, the
+literature audit, checksums, and reproduction instructions. We ask that both
+online resources be made available to the referees with the main manuscript.
+
+The manuscript is not under consideration elsewhere. All authors have
+approved the submission. The authors declare no competing interests. No
+research datasets were generated or analysed.
+
+Sincerely,
